Who I Am

About Me

Master's candidate in International Trade & Environment at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne, trained in econometrics, applied macroeconomics, and data-driven economic analysis. My work focuses on identifying causal relationships in complex economic systems and translating large-scale datasets into structured, decision-relevant insights using rigorous quantitative methods.

I also approach cross-border strategy and sustainability-related policy problems through structured analytical frameworks, integrating market dynamics, regulatory constraints, and operational considerations. My focus is on producing clear, evidence-based reasoning in ambiguous, data-intensive environments to support strategic decision-making.

Academic Work

Projects

Brexit Trade Impact Analysis

Econometrics · MSc Thesis

Brexit Trade Impact Analysis

DiD econometric model across 97 goods categories (UN Comtrade, 2012–2023) isolating the causal effect of Brexit from COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine. Validated through dual export/import estimation.

Supervised by Prof. Fontagné (CEPII) · Grade: 16/20

R StudioDiD ModelUN ComtradeEconometrics

Foreign Direct Investment in Kazakhstan

Analysis of FDI flows into Kazakhstan (2005–2022) across 10 source countries and 8 key sectors. Examined institutional factors, government initiatives, and the role of natural resources.

Economic Competitiveness of Switzerland

Macroeconomics · Research

Economic Competitiveness of Switzerland

Multi-layered analysis of Switzerland's economic competitiveness (1990s–present): TFP, R&D intensity, patent density, trade statistics (World Bank WITS). Four competitive pillars: innovation, processing model, trade integration, structural policy.

Co-authored with Yavuz Erim & Antoine Volland · Paris 1
